approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Registries Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would modernise Commonwealth business registers and introduce a director identification number (DIN).
A minister would choose an existing federal body to act as registrar, setting data standards and controlling how information is collected, stored and shared.

Directors of companies under the Corporations Act or CATSI Act would have to get a DIN from the registrar before being appointed, with extra time allowed in the first 12 months and for existing directors.
Modernise business registers by letting a minister appoint a registrar to run them under flexible, technology-neutral rules.
Introduce a requirement for company directors to obtain a director identification number from the registrar.
Create offences for unauthorised disclosure of information held by the registrar and for providing false identity information to the registrar.
Directors of bodies corporate registered under the Corporations Act and the CATSI Act, and officials handling registry information.

The bill creates core provisions for administering business registers under the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 and the A New Tax System (Australian Business Number) Act 1999, with these provisions mirrored in the Treasury Laws Amendment (Registries Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2019.

The bill introduces a single business register to integrate 32 existing registers into one platform administered by the Australian Business Registrar, and establishes a legal framework for a director identification number (DIN) that directors will keep permanently to prevent fictitious identities.
The bill allows the registrar to collect fees for registry services, supporting the Treasury Laws Amendment (Registries Modernisation and Other Measures) Bill 2019.

The legislation creates a single Commonwealth business register and introduces permanent director identification numbers (DINs) to track directors across companies, aiming to combat illegal phoenixing and modernise legacy registry systems.
